rv.q: This is a fine production with a first-rank cast that fills much of the void left by live theatre.

The restrained portrayal of the lovers’ passion is aesthetically brave, but there’s a downside: In his determination to eschew the easy charms of melodrama, Lloyd slightly undercooks the romance, which in turn diminishes our investment in its terrible ramifications.
Though to be fair, intense over-acting may be for the sake of the crowd, for whom Shakespeare remains a dense and daunting endeavor

The shining star of the evening is Toheeb Jimoh, aka Sam Obisanya in Ted Lasso. In silk shirt and with casual manner he brings something captivatingly conversational and excitingly quick-witted to his Romeo. One or two of the performers sound a bit constipated; Jimoh, by contrast, makes the metre
There is clarity throughout that demonstrates more than just how understandable Shakespeare is when done well.
